description: La mejor parte de leer es viajar sin estar presente, vivir historias de las que no seríamos parte sin la literatura. Absolutamente todo tiene un origen, del cual desconocemos tanto su legado como su contribución histórica. No basta con conocer la historia, sino vivirla, vivir en sus líneas. ¿Y cómo no vivirla si no es de la mano de un equipo amante de los astros y del espacio mismo?
summary:
The Elio Archives responds to the "Left Behind but Not Forgotten" challenge with three pieces that tell the story of NASA's space exploration in different formats: a digital comic, a web logbook, and a board game. It is designed for children, youth, and space enthusiasts.
The comic, Twenty-Eight Hours in a Smoky Room with a Red Clock, follows Elio, a fictional flight controller who experiences the decisive moments of Apollo 11 from the Houston control room, from the launch countdown to the astronauts' return. The events, timelines, and technical data are real. Elio serves to show the work of the people who made the journey possible.
ELIO's Logbook (NASA Explorer) is a web application to explore missions, vehicles, modules, and scientific instruments left on the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space. FORGOTTEN EXPEDITION takes that content into a board game to remember those missions by playing.
We start from one idea: the equipment left behind are not forgotten missions. Each one left discoveries and advancements that made subsequent exploration possible.
details:
Details
  • Digital Comic: This is the narrative piece. It features seven chapters and fifty panels. Elio follows the countdown, the Saturn V launch, the journey to the Moon, the descent of the Eagle module, the first moonwalk, the spacecraft rendezvous, and the return to Earth from Houston. By following the control team, the reader sees how the people behind the mission worked and the purpose of the systems, instruments, and vehicles they used.
  • ELIO's Logbook / NASA Explorer: This is the documentary piece: an interactive web application developed in 2026. It gathers information on missions, probes, rovers, modules, and scientific instruments that NASA sent into space. It allows users to learn what equipment was sent, its function, the discoveries it enabled, and where it remained after the mission ended. The content is drawn from NASA Science fact sheets and NSSDCA records listed in section 6. Anyone who finishes the comic can continue with other explorers that remain on the Moon, Mars, asteroids, and deep space.
  • FORGOTTEN EXPEDITION: This is a space board game to remember NASA's missions and exploration equipment. It turns historical and scientific data into a gameplay dynamic and is distributed as a PDF document.
Innovation Highlights
  • Uses a fictional character to bring the public closer to the real events of Apollo 11.
  • Unites a comic, documentary consultation, and board game in a single educational proposal.
  • Shows what equipment and artifacts remain on the Moon, Mars, and other places in the solar system.
  • Allows interactive exploration of information in the web logbook.
  • Uses the board game to reinforce the memory of the missions and their equipment.
